photos.alt: Boat deck heaped with crushed concrete cultch, a crewman walking alongside the pile, open bay on both sides
photos.caption: Load 25 aboard on 19 May 2025 — 89 short tons of crushed concrete, deck full and running out to the placement line.

photos.alt: A water cannon washing crushed concrete cultch off the side of the deck into the bay, spray over the rail
photos.caption: Load 27 going over the side, 20 May 2025. The wash cannon spreads the concrete along the planned track.

photos.alt: A full deck load of crushed concrete cultch, a crewman at the rail and the red wash hose in hand
photos.caption: The last load of the whole build, 7 June 2026 — 95 short tons staged with the wash hose already run out.

marsh.source: Adams Bay marsh loss, 2019-2024 (Sentinel-2 L2A + NAIP; NOAA CO-OPS 8761724)
marsh.steepest_cause: Hurricane Ida, 29 Aug 2021, Cat 4 at Port Fourchon (63 km W)
marsh.chronic: Every year in the record lost ground, including years with no landfall.
marsh.mechanism: Marsh erodes; the sediment it sheds moves into the water column and settles on the lease, burying shell. Not a loss of shelter.
marsh.limit: Optical imagery cannot see this bottom. The link is mechanistic, not a measured sediment flux.

caveats.detail: Classes firm exist only in the later survey. Before/after percentages mix real change with reclassification.
